candidate_tasks.title: Port commandSemantics command classifier
implementation_steps: Create gosrc/tools/bash_command_semantics.go.
Translate each classifier function 1:1: classifyTopLevel(cmd string), splitPipeline, classifyBuiltin, classifyExternal.

Build allow-list maps: readCommands (cat/ls/head/tail/grep/find/stat/git status/git diff/git log/jq/yq/wc/tree/file), networkCommands (curl/wget/nc/ssh/scp/rsync), destructiveCommands (rm/dd/mkfs/shred/format).
Expose ClassifyCommand(cmd string) CommandSemantic with stable enum values.
acceptance: Unit tests cover representative commands per category
Pipelines and chained commands (a && b; c | d) classified by worst category
candidate_tasks.notes: TS commandSemantics.ts:140 lines classifies a command into categories: 'read', 'write', 'network', 'process', 'destructive', 'unknown'. Used by readOnlyValidation and destructiveCommandWarning.

candidate_tasks.title: Port readOnlyValidation and route safe commands without confirmation
implementation_steps: Create gosrc/tools/bash_readonly.go.
Implement IsReadOnlyCommand(cmd string, semantics CommandSemantic) bool.
Cover edge cases: cd-only, env-only, echo-only, command substitution chains, pipelines where every element is read-only, here-string redirects to /dev/null only.
In BashTool.Execute, call IsReadOnlyCommand before any permission gate; if true, bypass permission handler.
Add tests for ~30 representative commands from TS test suite.
acceptance: ls, git status, jq '.' file.json bypass permission
rm -rf, npm install, curl POST do NOT bypass
Pipeline 'cat a | grep b' bypasses, 'cat a | tee b' does not
candidate_tasks.notes: TS readOnlyValidation.ts:1990 lines decides whether a command is read-only. Read-only commands skip permission prompts entirely.

candidate_tasks.title: Port pathValidation for boundary checking
implementation_steps: Create gosrc/tools/bash_path_validation.go.
Implement ExtractPathsFromCommand(cmd string) []string by tokenising the command (respecting quotes, command substitution, redirections).
Resolve relative paths against the BashTool.CWD.
Implement ValidatePathsAgainstAllowedDirs(paths []string, allowedDirs []string) error.
Wire into Execute pre-flight: if any extracted path is outside allowed_dirs, reject.
acceptance: Command 'cat /etc/passwd' rejected when allowed_dirs is ~/work
Command 'cat ./local.txt' resolves against CWD and is accepted if CWD is allowed
Quoted paths with spaces are extracted correctly
candidate_tasks.notes: TS pathValidation.ts:1303 lines extracts every absolute/relative path referenced in a command and checks against allowed_dirs.

candidate_tasks.title: Port sedEditParser to recognise implicit edits
implementation_steps: Create gosrc/tools/bash_sed_parser.go.
Implement ParseSedEdit(cmd string) (*SedEditPlan, bool) returning {FilePath, Edits: []{Op:'s'|'d'|'i'|'a', Pattern, Replacement, Flags}}.
Handle: in-place flag (-i with optional backup ext), multiple -e expressions, semicolon-separated programs, address ranges (e.g. '1,5d').
Add unit tests for at least 15 sed invocation variants.
acceptance: sed -i 's/foo/bar/g' file.txt parsed
sed -i.bak '1,5d;s/x/y/' file.txt parsed
sed without -i returns nil (read-only, no edit)
candidate_tasks.notes: TS sedEditParser.ts:322 lines parses 'sed -i s/old/new/g file.txt' into a virtual {filePath, oldString, newString} so it can run through the same readFileState/permission gate as the Edit tool.

candidate_tasks.title: Apply sed-edit through readFileState and Edit gating
implementation_steps: Create gosrc/tools/bash_sed_validation.go.
Before exec: if ParseSedEdit returns plan, look up readFileState entry for plan.FilePath.
If missing or stale (mtime mismatch), return error mirroring FileEditTool message: 'Read the file first using the Read tool. The Bash sed command will modify file <path>.'
After exec, update readFileState mtime so subsequent Edit calls succeed.
Add integration test driving a sed -i flow.
acceptance: sed -i without prior Read is rejected
Read+sed+Edit sequence works
External modification between Read and sed is detected
candidate_tasks.notes: TS sedValidation.ts:684 enforces 'must Read first' on the file sed will modify, mirroring FileEditTool semantics.

candidate_tasks.title: Port destructiveCommandWarning two-step confirmation
implementation_steps: Create gosrc/tools/bash_destructive_warning.go.
Implement DestructiveCommandWarning(cmd string) (warning string, requireConfirm bool).
Patterns to flag: rm -rf /, rm -rf ~, dd if=*, mkfs.*, shred -*, > /dev/sd*, find ... -exec rm.
In Execute: when warning fires and PermissionHandler is non-nil, request explicit confirmation via PermissionHandler.AskUser; in non-interactive mode return error.
Add tests.
acceptance: 'rm -rf /' triggers confirmation
'ls -la' does not
Confirmation respects PermissionHandler
candidate_tasks.notes: TS destructiveCommandWarning.ts:102 lines surfaces an extra confirmation prompt for rm -rf, dd, mkfs, etc.

candidate_tasks.title: Port shouldUseSandbox per-command toggle
implementation_steps: Add ShouldUseSandbox(cmd string, semantics CommandSemantic, hint string) bool to bash_readonly.go or new file.
Default true; return false for confirmed read-only commands AND when no path-validation flags raised.
In buildCommand, gate sandbox usage by this function plus existing dangerouslyDisableSandbox.
Add tests.
acceptance: Read-only commands skip sandbox by default
Network or write commands keep sandbox
dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true still wins
candidate_tasks.notes: TS shouldUseSandbox.ts:153 decides whether a command needs sandbox or can run unsandboxed (e.g. read-only commands skip sandbox for performance).

candidate_tasks.title: Port modeValidation for plan/yolo/safe modes
implementation_steps: Create gosrc/tools/bash_mode_validation.go.
Implement ValidateCommandForMode(cmd string, semantics CommandSemantic, mode string) error.
Modes: 'plan' (only read), 'safe' (no destructive), 'yolo' (no checks).
Wire in BashTool.Execute reading mode from PlanState/AppState.
acceptance: Plan mode blocks any non-read command
Safe mode blocks rm -rf
Yolo mode permits everything
candidate_tasks.notes: TS modeValidation.ts:115 lines blocks certain commands in plan mode (writes, network) and relaxes in yolo mode.

candidate_tasks.title: Port full bashSecurity command-injection detector
implementation_steps: Create gosrc/tools/bash_security.go.
Translate the rule list 1:1, organised as a slice of {Name, Pattern (regexp), Severity, Reason} entries.
Cover: $(echo cmd | base64 -d | sh), eval $arg, curl ... | sh, wget ... | bash, /dev/tcp redirection, exec </dev/tcp, perl/python -e payloads, hex/octal encoding, history -c.
Replace existing DetectDangerousCommand with the richer engine.
Add table-driven tests with at least 30 positive and 20 negative cases.
acceptance: Pipe-to-shell variants are flagged
Common legitimate complex commands (e.g. 'find . -name foo -print0 | xargs -0 grep bar') are NOT flagged
Severity levels expose blocking vs warning policy
candidate_tasks.notes: TS bashSecurity.ts:2592 lines is the heaviest module: detects shell metacharacter injection, encoded command tricks, $() abuse, base64-decoded payloads. Current Go DetectDangerousCommand is far thinner.

candidate_tasks.title: Port bashPermissions rule-matching engine
implementation_steps: Create gosrc/tools/bash_permissions.go.
Define rule grammar: 'Bash(<name>[:<args>][!])' where ! denies and absence allows.
Implement MatchBashRule(cmd string, rules []permissions.Rule) (decision Decision, matchedRule *permissions.Rule).
Decision is Allow / Deny / NeedAsk.
Wire into Execute: pre-flight rule check before invoking sandbox.
Hook into existing permissions package; reuse PermissionRule type if already present.
Add tests for rule patterns: literal match, prefix wildcard, deny override, allow-all '*'.
acceptance: 'Bash(npm test)' allows 'npm test' but not 'npm install'
'Bash(git:*)' allows 'git status', 'git push'
Deny rule overrides allow rule
No matching rule returns NeedAsk
candidate_tasks.notes: TS bashPermissions.ts:2621 matches a bash invocation against settings.json permission rules: 'Bash(npm test)', 'Bash(git:*)', 'Bash(rm:!)' etc.

candidate_tasks.title: Strengthen background task lifecycle and output protocol
implementation_steps: Audit gosrc/tools/background_tasks.go to confirm output path lifecycle.
Cap output file at 50MB with rotation suffix .1.
Emit final-state line on completion: 'TASK_FINISHED exit=<code> duration=<ms>'.
Surface task completion through hooks Runner so harness can re-trigger model.
Add integration test: background long-running command, read output mid-flight, then read after completion.
acceptance: Output file truncates gracefully on overflow
Final TASK_FINISHED line present
Hook receives task-completion event
candidate_tasks.notes: TS BashTool background tasks emit stdout to a tracked file; Go has BackgroundTaskManager but lacks size cap, rotation, timeout and final 'task-notification' integration.

candidate_tasks.title: Wire commandSemantics + readOnly into ToolResult metadata
implementation_steps: Extend ToolResult.Metadata (string-map) on Bash returns with these fields.
Ensure consumers (registry, analytics, hooks) read them without crashing if missing.
Add tests verifying metadata for at least 5 commands.
acceptance: Bash result includes the metadata fields
Existing consumers do not break
candidate_tasks.notes: TS attaches metadata to BashTool result like {wasReadOnly:bool, semanticCategory:string} for analytics + UI.

candidate_tasks.title: End-to-end Bash conformance test against TS golden fixtures
implementation_steps: Mirror TS test cases from src/tools/BashTool/__tests__/ (or describe blocks) into gosrc/tools/bash_conformance_test.go as table-driven cases listing command+expected (decision, semantic, readOnly).
Skip cases dependent on TS-only services; document each skip with reason.
Add `go test ./tools -run TestBashConformance` and require it green.
acceptance: ≥80 conformance cases pass
Documented skips < 10
